findings.detail: The native bridge now caps pending output to 512 KiB / 1024 frames and schedules one drain plus at most one overflow closure. Tested actual compiled Post method with 5000 queued submissions and unexecuted dispatcher callbacks.
ElevatedSession and ConPty teardown now each use Interlocked.Exchange to establish one native-handle teardown owner.

Each status/admission verifies a bounded, strict, unique-entry version-9.8.7 runtime seal against the exact helper byte count and SHA256; full ancestor symbolic link checks run before and after reads.
Timeout and busy-target results use unique bridge request IDs independent of the delegate job ID. Bounded native acknowledgment history now records these outgoing controls.
A lifetime lock now serializes ResizePseudoConsole against detaching HPCON for asynchronous close. Close itself runs after releasing the lock.

checks.scope: Controlled native child and native-message fixtures only. Performed before the final unique internal request ID change.

checks.suite: Final changed timeout and busy-target ACK paths
checks.scope: Includes actual-helper-style acknowledgments and unique internal IDs.

checks.scope: No Windows elevation is started; matching pending request cancellation only.

checks.scope: Reflection invokes pure boundary predicates and queues dispatcher callbacks without running them or creating a WebView window.

limitations: No Administrator UAC consent or elevated PowerShell startup is claimed by this audit.
Actual ConPTY process and PowerShell integration are validated separately by the transport agent.
The working runtime seal currently lacks the newly compiled helper; release packaging must regenerate it before Administrator admission is available.

Minimal cross-process named-pipe tests could not complete on this tool host; raw Win32 open returned access denied. Do not label native PowerShell-to-XPU delegation end-to-end verified from these fixtures.

pipeDiagnostics.constructorVerdict: Both original New-Object shorthand and explicit ArgumentList construct the correct stream and normalize the exact expected pipe path.
pipeDiagnostics.interpretation: A Windows permission boundary prevents these diagnostic child clients from opening the listening pipe. This is not evidence of a constructor or ConPTY path defect. The precise source of the denial is not proven by the diagnostic.
